newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-SANTORO TOPPLES ANOTHER CLAY COURT SPECIALIST.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SANTORO TOPPLES ANOTHER CLAY COURT SPECIALIST.

text.p: Frenchman Fabrice Santoro notched his second consecutive upset at the Monte Carlo tennis Open on Thursday, toppling Spain's Sergi Bruguera in three sets two days after beating Austrian Thomas Muster.

With his 3-6 7-5 6-1 victory over the tournament's 16th seed, Santoro has defeated two of the best clay court specialists in the world, both former French Open champions who between them also won five titles here.
"I had not won many matches coming here so these two victories are very important to me," said the 24-year-old Frenchman, currently ranked a modest 90th in the world.
"I rank them among the three or four best wins in my career."
Another Spanish favourite, Albert Costa, bid an early farewell to the tournament. Costa, losing finalist in the principality last year, was beaten by Chile's Marcelo Rios 7-6 6-4.
Even more than the result was the way Santoro beat Bruguera which came as a surprise.

The short Frenchman used to be a typical clay court player, making up for his lack of power by a lot of running behind the baseline. Against a lacklustre Bruguera, he rushed to the net 61 times, scoring fine volleys like a player bred on grass.
"This year I realised I could not go on like that if I wanted to make a career. I was a ball fiddler. My game belonged to the 70's more than to the 90's," he said.
"I realised I did not have enough power to score from the baseline so I decided to try my luck at the net. Now I feel comfortable there."
After a fine first set, which he won 6-3, Bruguera suddenly fell apart. Despite winning his serve back twice in the second set, he used up a lot of stamina in a vain uphill battle.
It seemed as though the Spaniard had no strength left in a one-sided third set, in which he saved one match point before bowing 6-1.
Rios took a sweet revenge over Costa in the first match of the day.
The 21-year-old Chilean, who lost to Costa in the semifinals last year, won 7-6 6-4 in a match which should be a big morale booster for him as the clay court season gears up.
In the quarter-finals, Rios, the seventh seed, will meet Sweden's Magnus Larsson, who ousted American world number one Pete Sampras in the previous round.
Larsson eased past Czech Daniel Vacek 7-5 6-0.

"I was born on clay, I like to play on clay but when you play as well as I did today, the surface doesn't matter," said Rios, who has had a lacklustre season so far, reaching only one ATP Tour final, in Marseille in February.
Spaniard Alex Corretja survived a tense battle against Czech Bohdan Ulihrach. The 12th seed, winner in Estoril two weeks ago, won 4-6 7-6 6-0.
